item.title: MIT's AI model suggests recipes for making new materials
item.description:
MIT researchers have developed an AI model called DiffSyn that can suggest promising synthesis routes for complex materials, addressing one of the most time-consuming bottlenecks in materials science. The tool, described in a paper published today in Nature Computational Science, demonstrated state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting pathways for creating zeolites, a class of materials with applications in catalysis, absorption, and ion exchange processes.

"To use an analogy, we know what kind of cake we want to make, but right now we don't know how to bake the cake," said lead author Elton Pan, a PhD candidate in MIT's Department of Materials Science and Engineering. "Materials synthesis is currently done through domain expertise and trial and error."

item.title: ConocoPhillips CEO projects global LNG market to double by 2050
item.description: Speaking at the LNG2026 conference in Doha, Qatar, ConocoPhillips Chairman and CEO Ryan Lance forecasted that the global liquefied natural gas market will double by mid-century, reaching 800 million tons from approximately 400 million tons today. The remarks underscore the energy giant's bullish outlook on natural gas as a critical fuel source for the coming decades.

item.title: Trump launches $12B critical minerals stockpile to counter China
item.description:
President Donald Trump is set to launch Project Vault, a $12 billion initiative aimed at establishing a first-of-its-kind strategic critical minerals stockpile for the private sector, according to Bloomberg. The venture combines $1.67 billion in private capital with a $10 billion loan from the US Export-Import Bank to procure and store minerals for automakers, technology firms, and other manufacturers reliant on rare earths and other metals.

The initiative represents the Trump administration's most aggressive effort yet to insulate American manufacturers from supply shocks and reduce reliance on Chinese-controlled supply chains. Details of the program were described by senior administration officials, though specifics about which minerals will be prioritized and where they will be stored have not been disclosed.

item.title: Pakistan says forces killed 145 militants in Balochistan
item.description:
Pakistan's security forces killed 145 militants over a 40-hour period following a wave of coordinated attacks across the southwestern province of Balochistan, marking one of the deadliest flare-ups in the region's decades-long separatist insurgency.

The violence, which erupted on Saturday across more than a dozen locations, left 17 law enforcement personnel and 31 civilians dead, according to Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, who addressed reporters in the provincial capital Quetta on Sunday.

"We managed to kill 145 terrorists in 40 hours," Bugti said, describing the toll as the highest militant casualties in such a short span since Pakistan began its counterterrorism campaign. "The bodies of these 145 killed terrorists are in our custody, and some of them are Afghan nationals."

item.title: Colombia's Petro arrives in Washington for Trump summit
item.description: Colombian President Gustavo Petro arrived in Washington over the weekend ahead of his first face-to-face meeting with President Donald Trump, scheduled for Tuesday at the White House. The encounter aims to reset a bilateral relationship that has badly frayed over months of escalating tensions between two leaders known for their unpredictable natures.

item.title: SpaceX in advanced talks to merge with xAI, sources say
item.description: Elon Musk is moving rapidly to consolidate his business empire as SpaceX and artificial intelligence firm xAI have entered advanced discussions to merge, according to Bloomberg. The companies have already informed some of their investors about the plans, with an agreement potentially coming as soon as this week.

item.title: QatarEnergy CEO says AI demand may flip LNG glut to shortage
item.description:
Rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence and data centers could flip the global liquefied natural gas market from projected oversupply to shortage by the end of the decade, QatarEnergy CEO Saad al-Kaabi warned at the opening of the LNG2026 conference in Doha on Monday.

"We always thought the market would have some kind of oversupply between 2025-2030 and beyond 2030 you will have a shortage," al-Kaabi said, adding that demand expectations have increased "mainly due to AI and data center requirements, which are sustained power requirements as a baseload."

The warning comes as a record wave of LNG supply begins flowing from major projects in the United States and Qatar between 2026 and 2029, which had raised concerns among analysts about a supply glut that could depress prices. Projects like Golden Pass LNG on the U.S. Gulf Coast and Qatar's North Field Expansion are expected to contribute sizable new volumes.

item.title: US-Iran nuclear talks planned for Friday in Istanbul
item.description:
Turkey, Qatar, and Egypt are working to arrange urgent diplomatic talks between White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, with a meeting planned for Friday in Istanbul, as escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran raise fears of a broader regional conflict.

The diplomatic push comes as Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei warned Sunday that any U.S. attack would not remain limited. "The Americans should know that if they start a war, this time it will be a regional war," Khamenei said during a public address in Tehran. His comments followed the deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group to the Arabian Sea, which President Donald Trump has characterized as a "massive armada".

item.title: Trump cuts India tariffs to 18% after Modi pledges to halt Russian oil
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Monday that the United States and India have reached an immediate trade deal following a phone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, lowering reciprocal tariffs from 25% to 18%. Under the agreement, India committed to stop buying Russian oil and purchase over $500 billion in US energy, technology, agricultural, and other products.

The breakthrough marks a potential turning point in bilateral relations that had grown strained over the past year, with the US imposing steep 50% tariffs on Indian exports—among the highest applied to any country—in August 2025.

item.title: Anthropic partners with Allen Institute, HHMI on AI for science
item.description:
Anthropic announced two new partnerships with the Allen Institute and Howard Hughes Medical Institute on Monday, signaling the AI company's deepening push into life sciences as it seeks to embed Claude-powered agents into scientific research workflows.

The collaborations, announced in an exclusive report by Fortune, will see the elite science labs use Anthropic's technology to address analysis, annotation, and coordination bottlenecks that can stretch research timelines into years. Rather than focusing on AI breakthroughs akin to Google DeepMind's AlphaFold, Anthropic is betting that its AI agents can accelerate the unglamorous but time-consuming work between discoveries.

item.title: OpenAI launches Codex desktop app for running parallel AI coding agents
item.description:
OpenAI on Monday unveiled a dedicated macOS desktop application for its Codex AI coding assistant, introducing what the company calls a "command center for agents" that enables software developers to run multiple AI coding assistants in parallel on long-running tasks.

The Codex app, available starting today, marks a departure from the command-line and browser-based interfaces that developers have used since Codex launched in April 2025. According to OpenAI, the desktop application is designed to address a fundamental shift in how developers work with AI—from pair programming with a single assistant to orchestrating teams of autonomous agents across projects.

"This is the most loved internal product we've ever had," CEO Sam Altman said during a press briefing ahead of the launch. "It's been totally an amazing thing for us to be using recently at OpenAI".

item.title: Iran summons EU ambassadors over terror designation of Guard
item.description:
Iran summoned all European Union ambassadors in the country to formally protest the bloc's designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, escalating diplomatic tensions between Tehran and Brussels at a time of heightened regional instability.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei confirmed Monday that the summoning process began Sunday and continued into Monday, calling the EU's decision "illegal, unreasonable and very wrong." Baghaei said Iranian authorities are preparing reciprocal actions that will be sent to "decision-making bodies" in the coming days.

item.title: Iran's president orders nuclear talks with US amid threats
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the start of nuclear negotiations with the United States on Monday, with talks expected in Turkey in the coming days as both nations step back from the brink of military confrontation. The directive comes after weeks of escalating tensions following Iran's deadly crackdown on anti-government protests and President Donald Trump's deployment of an aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East.

item.title: New transparent windows can shield buildings from EMP attacks
item.description:
Researchers from South Korea and the United States have developed transparent glass windows capable of shielding buildings from electromagnetic pulse threats, addressing a critical gap in defense technology for civilian and military infrastructure.

The breakthrough, led by Professor Chang Won Jung from the Department of Semiconductor Engineering at Seoul National University of Science and Technology (SeoulTech), employs an asymmetric hexagonal metal mesh film structure that delivers EMP protection while maintaining optical transparency. The research was published in Volume 72 of Engineering Science and Technology, an International Journal in December 2025.

item.title: UK's Mandelson quits Labour as Epstein files trigger global fallout
item.description:
The U.S. Department of Justice on Friday released over three million pages of documents, 180,000 images, and more than 2,000 videos from its investigation into convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, triggering resignations and political turmoil across multiple countries.

The massive disclosure, mandated by the Epstein Files Transparency Act signed by President Donald Trump in November 2025, represents the most extensive release since Congress passed the bipartisan legislation by overwhelming margins. Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said Friday's release marked "the end of a very comprehensive document identification and review process."

item.title: Glencore nears Citi appointment for Rio Tinto merger talks
item.description:
Swiss miner Glencore is close to engaging Citigroup as its lead investment bank on its potential acquisition by Rio Tinto, a deal that could create the world's largest mining company worth over $200 billion, according to Reuters citing two people familiar with the matter.

Citigroup Global Markets Inc. filed disclosures with the UK Takeover Panel in January, identifying itself as connected with Glencore in relation to a possible deal with Rio Tinto, according to filings made at the London Stock Exchange. Both Citi and Glencore declined to comment on the appointment.

item.title: NASA pauses Artemis II fueling test after hydrogen leak detected
item.description:
NASA is conducting a high-stakes fueling test of its massive moon rocket Monday as the agency pushes toward the first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years, though engineers have encountered a hydrogen leak that required troubleshooting during the critical rehearsal.

The wet dress rehearsal, which began Saturday evening at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, simulates launch day procedures by loading the 322-foot Space Launch System rocket with more than 700,000 gallons of super-cold liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. If successful, the Artemis II mission could launch as early as February 8, sending four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon.

item.title: German researchers develop AI drones to locate radioactive waste in minutes
item.description:
Researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Communication, Information Processing and Ergonomics FKIE in Germany have developed AI-powered drones and robots capable of locating radioactive sources within a few meters in just minutes, addressing one of the most dangerous challenges facing emergency responders.

The technology, unveiled this week, aims to protect first responders and civilians from the invisible threat posed by chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosive substances (CBRNE) that cannot be detected by humans from a safe distance.

item.title: Wall Street rises as oil, gold slide on US-Iran diplomatic thaw
item.description:
Wall Street rebounded Monday as diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran unwound the geopolitical risk premiums that had driven commodity prices higher in recent weeks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more than 500 points while crude oil tumbled more than 4% and precious metals extended a historic rout.

The rally came after President Donald Trump said over the weekend that Iran was "seriously talking" with Washington, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the resumption of nuclear negotiations. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to meet White House envoy Steve Witkoff on Friday in Istanbul for the first direct engagement between U.S. and Iranian officials since the collapse of talks and the 12-day conflict in June 2025.

item.title: Musk confirms SpaceX-xAI merger ahead of planned IPO
item.description:
Elon Musk is combining his rocket and satellite company SpaceX with his artificial intelligence firm xAI in a corporate consolidation that could set the stage for one of the largest initial public offerings in history. The deal was announced via internal memo on Monday, according to Bloomberg News, bringing together Musk's space exploration infrastructure with his AI ambitions under a single corporate umbrella.

The newly combined entity is expected to be valued at approximately $1.25 trillion, with a share price set around $527, according to Reuters citing Bloomberg's reporting. The merger comes as SpaceX prepares for a mid-June IPO that could raise as much as $50 billion and value the company at roughly $1.5 trillion, according to the Financial Times.
